profile.stagger_pattern: ANNUAL elections on the Texas uniform date (first Saturday in May), 2-year terms, two staggered groups. EVEN years (2018, 2020, 2022, 2024, 2026): Mayor + Position 1 + Position 5. ODD years (2017, 2019, 2021, 2023, 2025): Positions 2, 3, 4. Confirmed by the city's own Elections page (2027 ballot = Positions 2, 3 and 4) and by which Shenandoah races appear in each Montgomery County canvass.

run_log.detail: Texas registry entry MEDIUM. Its Montgomery County lead - elections.mctx.org publishing canvass PDFs directly - is LIVE and was the single highest-yield source for this city. The registry's constructible path 'https://elections.mctx.org/results/{YEAR}_{MONTH}_{Description}.pdf' is correct but the {Description} segment is not guessable; the archive index at https://elections.mctx.org/ElectionResults.asp lists every canvass 2006-2026 as plain hrefs in server-rendered HTML and should be scraped instead of constructed. Registry warning that city races are bundled into joint county reports held: Shenandoah appears inside 'Joint Election Canvass Report' PDFs, never in a city-named file.

CENSUS VERDICT WRONG. The census recorded Shenandoah as having no working archive because the site had 'moved to shenandoahpdtx.gov' and both domains were robots-blocked. In fact shenandoahpdtx.gov is the POLICE DEPARTMENT site (pd = police department), not a relocated city site; the city site is https://www.shenandoahtx.us and it returned HTTP 200 to plain curl with a browser UA on the first request. Its robots.txt disallows only /admin, /search.asp and similar - not the archive. Every city document used here came from that domain.

STRUCTURE SETTLED FROM THE CITY'S OWN PAGES, no search cost. https://www.shenandoahtx.us/337/Election: 'The City's General Election for members of the City Council is held annually on the first Saturday in May' and names Positions 2, 3 and 4 as the seats on the 2027 ballot. https://www.shenandoahtx.us/220/City-Council: General Law (Type A) city, council-manager form with an appointed city administrator, 'an elected City Council of five members and a Mayor'. Therefore: 2-year terms, ANNUAL elections, two staggered groups - Mayor+P1+P5 in even years, P2+P3+P4 in odd years - i.e. EIGHT cycles in the 2019-2026 panel, not two. The mayor is DIRECTLY ELECTED despite the council-manager form (confirmed by Shenandoah Mayor races appearing on the 2018, 2022 and 2026 county canvasses).

Montgomery County joint-election canvass PDFs, downloaded with curl and extracted locally with 'pdftotext -layout' (WebFetch never used on them). Shenandoah races found in 2017, 2018, 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2026 May canvasses. COLUMN-MAPPING TRAP: in these canvasses candidate names are rotated 90 degrees, so pdftotext emits them on separate lines in an order that does NOT match the vote columns - the mapping is by horizontal indent (leftmost name = leftmost number). Reading them in line order reverses the 2019 Position 2 result. Verified the indent rule against three races with independently known outcomes (2021 P3 Escoto, 2022 Mayor Escoto, 2026 P5 Robinson) before trusting it.

ADOPTED BUDGET SERIES IS THE ANNUAL ROSTER SOURCE FOR THIS CITY. https://www.shenandoahtx.us/177/Budget-Documents-Information links every adopted budget FY2014-15 through FY2026-27. Each one carries BOTH a 'CITY COUNCIL' cover page listing Mayor and Positions 1-5 by name AND a statutory 'Record Vote' page listing every member present by name and position - a September snapshot for every panel year. This is what filled the three cycles the county canvass structurally could not (2020, 2024, 2025 - see below). It does not name the mayor pro tem.

THREE CYCLES HAD NO BALLOT: Shenandoah is absent from the May 2020, May 2024 and May 2025 Montgomery County canvasses, and from November 2020. This is the 'unopposed, not missing' pattern the brief warns about, in its Texas form - Tex. Elec. Code s.2.053 lets a city cancel an election when every candidate is unopposed. Confirmed for 2024 verbatim: 'Council voted 5-0 to approve an ordinance canceling the May 4 Municipal election' (Woodlands Online, 2024-03-01). Confirmed for 2025 by Community Impact ('Shenandoah, Oak Ridge North to see uncontested elections in May', 2025-02-18) plus the FY2025-26 adopted budget roster. Inferred for 2020 from the FY2020-21 adopted budget showing the identical Mayor/P1/P5 trio after the uniform date - those three rows are marked confidence 'medium' because no cancellation order itself was retrieved.

THREE mid-term changes found, all dated. (1) 2022-05-07: John G. Escoto, elected to Position 3 in May 2021, won the mayoralty - recorded as exit_mode 'elevated' on P3 and entry_mode 'succeeded' on the mayoralty. P3 sat vacant until 2022-06-22, when council appointed Jim Pollard 3-1 from 16 applicants for the remaining ~10 months (Community Impact, 2022-06-22; 2022-06-22 was a Wednesday, matching the 2nd/4th-Wednesday meeting rule). (2) 2024-11-05: Ted Fletcher resigned Position 2 citing 'personal and professional reasons'; Mayor Escoto nominated Joe Summerlin, approved unanimously 2024-11-13, sworn in 2024-12-11 (Community Impact, 2024-11-14 and 2024-12-12; both dates are Wednesdays). Summerlin then ran unopposed in the cancelled May 2025 election. (3) 2024-05-04: Michael 'Mike' McLeod left Position 5 at term end rather than mid-term - he is on the roll call through 2024-02-28 and Frank Robinson is in the seat by 2024-06-26. The two short vacancies (P3, 2022-05-07 to 2022-06-22; P2, 2024-11-05 to 2024-12-11) are NOT filed as gaps: both fall inside seat-years already covered by tenure rows, so filing them would emit contradictory panel rows.

CONTRADICTION FOUND AND RESOLVED IN THE CITY'S OWN PRESS RELEASE. The 2024 election-cancellation notice (Woodlands Online 78038, verbatim) says 'The Mayor and Councilmember Place 5 drew no opposition. The open position of Councilmember Place 1 drew one candidate. Congratulations to Mayor John Escoto and Councilmember Place 1 Ron Raymaker on re-election. Congratulations to new Councilmember Place 1 Elect Frank Robinson.' It assigns Place 1 to two different people. Two independent sources settle it against the release: the FY2024-25 adopted budget record vote (September 2024) lists 'Ron Raymaker, Position 1' and 'Frank W.Robinson, Position 5', and the May 2026 county canvass has Robinson on the ballot for Position 5. Robinson took Position 5; the release mislabels it. Recorded accordingly.

Roster cross-check: county canvass, adopted-budget record votes and news attendance lists agree on every seat in every year they overlap. Seat count is constant at 6 (Mayor + Positions 1-5) across the whole panel. Every name recorded here came from locally extracted PDF text or from raw HTML fetched with curl and stripped locally - the page-summarizing layer was used only to locate documents, never as the source of a name, except the two Community Impact articles (Pollard appointment, Fletcher resignation), whose key facts were each corroborated by a second independent source (FY2022-23 and FY2025-26 budget rosters respectively).

MAYOR PRO TEM is the only unresolved element. Charlie Bradt (Position 4) is sourced as mayor pro tem on 2023-05-10, 2023-07-26, 2024-02-28, 2024-06-26 (Woodlands Online attendance lines) and in the FY2026-27 proposed budget record-vote table ('Charlie Bradt, Mayor Pro-Tem, Position 4'), so his 2023-05-10-to-present tenure is recorded once at confidence 'medium' (2025 is bridged by continuity between dated observations either side of it). For 2019-2022 the office could not be sourced: AgendaCenter minutes ids below ~400 are purged (404 on both Minutes and ArchivedMinutes), the 2022 minutes that do exist are image-only PDFs with no text layer, the CivicPlus site search /Search/Results?searchPhrase= returned only 4 results and no archive depth, the AgendaCenter dated search /AgendaCenter/Search/?term=&CIDs=12,13&startDate=&endDate= returned zero documents, and /AgendaCenter/UpdateCategoryList 404s. Four gap rows filed.

48 of 48 elected seat-years (6 seats x 8 years) sourced. Mayor Pro Tem tracked as a 7th seat: 4 of 8 seat-years sourced, 4 in gaps. Zero low-confidence rows; 4 medium-confidence rows (the three 2020 cancelled-election tenures and the mayor pro tem row).
